interest: This file is valuable to historians of the Allied Occupation of Japan for illustrating the operational tension between democratic reform and food security. It reveals the behind-the-scenes diplomatic coordination among the State Department, the Department of the Army, SCAP, and the British delegation over Far Eastern Commission policy (C4-277 series), highlighting U.S. concerns that sudden decontrol of agricultural associations could disrupt crucial postwar food collection and distribution. Furthermore, the detailed intelligence check sheet produced by SCAP's Natural Resources Section provides an authoritative contemporary baseline on rural conditions in early 1949: it documents the dismantling of the wartime totalitarian nōgyōkai and commercial control networks, details how village food committees and mayors allocated delivery quotas, explains household-level membership patterns under the new Agricultural Cooperative Association Law (Law 132 of 1947), and assesses rural resistance to Communist infiltration. The file is also noteworthy for the participation of key figures such as Robert A. Fearey and the young Edward G. Seidensticker, Jr., who drafted the transmitting despatch from Tokyo.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.5032) covers the formulation of Allied Occupation policy and subsequent field assessments regarding the reform, democratization, and administration of Japanese agricultural cooperatives and rural credit between July 1948 and April 1949. The early documents focus on Washington-level inter-office and inter-agency deliberations concerning the Far Eastern Commission (FEC) policy series C4-277 ("Principles for Japanese Farmers' Organizations"), specifically weighing proposed United Kingdom amendments that urged gradual implementation to avoid disrupting food collection against the imperative to eliminate wartime government regimentation. The later records, spanning January to April 1949, originate from an intelligence request by the State Department's Office of Intelligence Research (OIR) and transmit an extensive survey prepared by GHQ SCAP's Natural Resources Section. This survey elucidates the operational realities of the post-reform cooperative structure established under Law 132 of 1947, detailing the allocation of food delivery quotas, the dissolution and liquidation of the wartime agricultural associations (nōgyōkai) and control monopolies, cooperative membership criteria, coordination with SCAPIN 411 land reform directives, and the negligible inroads made by Communist elements among organized farmers.

subfiles.about: Formulates the Division of Northeast Asian Affairs' stance on Far Eastern Commission papers C4-277/5 and /8 regarding principles for Japanese agricultural cooperatives.
subfiles.from: John M. Allison (NA - Division of Northeast Asian Affairs)
subfiles.summary: John M. Allison informs Frank A. Schuler, Jr. of NA's position regarding Far Eastern Commission papers C4-277/5 and C4-277/8, following consideration of Mr. Kroll's July 1 memorandum. NA agrees to support the first British amendment calling for gradual implementation, but opposes the remaining two UK amendments. The memorandum recommends securing formal Army Department clearance and determining whether SCAP's approval is necessary before final U.S. adoption in the FEC.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Allison to Schuler on NA Position on Principles for Japanese Farmers' Organizations
subfiles.to: Frank A. Schuler, Jr. (ADO - Division of Occupied Area Affairs)

subfiles.about: Synthesizes expert and departmental viewpoints on British amendments to the FEC policy paper governing Japanese farmers' organizations.
subfiles.from: Mr. Kroll (Division of Occupied Area Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Mr. Kroll reports on a conference with Dr. Ward W. Fetrow of the Farm Credit Administration (formerly economic consultant to SCAP's Natural Resources Section) and collates opinions from departmental divisions (OE, C, O, and ADO) regarding the C4-277 series. The consensus favors adopting only the first UK amendment, which encourages gradual execution to avert food collection and distribution dislocations, while rejecting amendments that retain Japanese government inspection powers or make cooperatives informers against defaulting farmers. Kroll requests NA's views on Committee #4 strategy and on informing SCAP of the proceedings.
subfiles.title: Draft Memorandum from Kroll to Fearey on U.S. Position on FEC C4-277 Series
subfiles.to: Robert A. Fearey (Division of Northeast Asian Affairs)

subfiles.about: Requests field information from Tokyo concerning the functioning, quotas, organization, and political inclinations of Japanese agricultural cooperatives.
subfiles.from: Department of State (drafted by Stanley Nehmer, OIR-DRF)
subfiles.summary: The Department of State dispatches Outgoing Airgram A-13 to the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo, noting that available information on agricultural cooperatives created under the December 1947 legislation is insufficient. The airgram submits six detailed questions on village food delivery quota allocations, the growth of multiple cooperatives per village, the status of dissolved agricultural and sericulture associations, the role of cooperatives in land reform, statistical reporting of membership, and Communist influence. Responses are requested for the Acquisition and Distribution Division under reference IAD-163.
subfiles.title: State Department Outgoing Airgram A-13 to US POLAD Tokyo Requesting Information on Agricultural Cooperatives
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits GHQ SCAP Natural Resources Section data on Japanese agricultural cooperatives to the State Department in reply to Airgram A-13.
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: The Acting United States Political Adviser in Tokyo forwards Despatch No. 153 to the Secretary of State, referencing Department Airgram A-13 and Tokyo's interim Airgram A-22. The despatch transmits information compiled by GHQ SCAP's Natural Resources Section in response to Washington's inquiries regarding Japanese agricultural cooperatives. The document was prepared for transmission by Vice Consul Edward G. Seidensticker, Jr., with distribution designated for various economic, intelligence, and labor offices.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 153 from US POLAD Tokyo Transmitting NRS Report on Agricultural Cooperatives

subfiles.about: Answers State Department questions regarding food delivery quotas, cooperative autonomy, dissolution of nōgyōkai, and rural political dynamics in Japan.
subfiles.from: Natural Resources Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (GHQ SCAP)
subfiles.summary: The Natural Resources Section of GHQ SCAP delivers point-by-point answers to the six questions raised in State Department Airgram A-13. The report explains that village mayors and elected food committees allocate delivery quotas independently of cooperatives, which only act as commercial handling agents on commission. It clarifies the dissolution of wartime compulsory nōgyōkai and control monopolies, notes the establishment of approximately 30,000 democratic cooperatives under Law 132 of 1947, explains that dual and multi-member household registrations account for over 7.3 million memberships, links the reforms to SCAPIN 411, and concludes that Communist efforts to dominate cooperatives have made no meaningful progress.
subfiles.title: GHQ SCAP Natural Resources Section Check Sheet on Japanese Agricultural Cooperatives
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Records that Tokyo Despatch No. 153 fully satisfies the inquiry in Airgram A-13 and authorizes filing.
subfiles.from: Stanley Nehmer (DRF - Division of Research for Far East)
subfiles.summary: Stanley Nehmer of the Division of Research for Far East (DRF) submits State Department Form DS-10 (Reference Slip) to the Division of Communications and Records (DC/R). He notes that no further departmental action is required because Tokyo's Despatch No. 153 provides a full and complete reply to Airgram A-13 of January 19, 1949.
subfiles.title: State Department Reference Slip from Stanley Nehmer to DC/R
subfiles.to: Division of Communications and Records (DC/R), Department of State
